## Full narration per scene (review pass)

S1 (Hook). You can lock onto a single stock — Tesla, Nvidia, the next one — and ride it hard. Sometimes it works. Mostly the volatility eats you, or the next great story turns out to be the last one. The Family Fund starts from the opposite premise. We don't pick the winner. We build a structure that doesn't need a winner to be right.

S2 (Why the index). Most active managers don't beat the S&P 500 over a decade. The index is already a broad, low-cost bet on the U.S. economy — five hundred companies, one ticker. So the fund's growth sleeve starts from the index, not from a hand-picked stock. If you can't reliably out-pick five hundred companies, you stop trying.

S3 (3x twist — capital efficiency). There are leveraged ETFs that aim to move at three times the daily index. Most people see them as a way to bet harder. The fund uses them differently — as a capital-efficiency tool. Three times exposure in one third of the capital. That's not louder. That's smaller, with the same market footprint.

S4 (Math: $33 + $67 freed). A hundred dollars in the S&P, all in. Or, roughly thirty-three dollars in a three-times S&P ETF, plus sixty-seven dollars freed up. Same market exposure on the index, two thirds of the cash uncommitted. The freed cash isn't profit — it's optionality. Room to hold gold, cash, crypto, the rest of the portfolio.

S5 (Decay caveat). Leveraged ETFs have a real cost. They reset daily, so in choppy markets they decay relative to the underlying. They are not set-and-forget. The fund treats them as an active sleeve — sized small, watched closely, rebalanced. The leverage is a tool, not a position you marry.

S6 (Buckets 40/45/15). Inspired by Ray Dalio's All Seasons portfolio — built to hold up in expansion, recession, inflation, deflation — the fund splits into three buckets. Forty percent Growth: the leveraged index sleeve. Forty-five percent Stability: cash and gold. Fifteen percent Crypto: Ethereum and Bitcoin. One number per bucket. Easy to maintain. Easy to explain.

S7 (Sector tilt — conviction, not forecast). Inside the growth bucket, the fund tilts. Alongside leveraged S&P, there's leveraged technology and leveraged semiconductors. That tilt is a personal conviction — that tech and semis stay structurally important. It's not a forecast. It's not expected outperformance. It's a discretionary view, sized small, and labelled honestly.

S8 (Aggressive/Defensive dial). How aggressive the fund is comes down to one knob — the percent in the leveraged growth sleeve. Higher means more market exposure with less cash committed, and more decay risk on the way. Lower means the fund leans defensive — more gold, more cash, fewer surprises. The knob is the policy. Everything else is execution.

S9 (Rebalancing bridge). Once a quarter — or whenever the buckets drift far enough — the fund rebalances. That cadence does two jobs at once. It trims runaway leverage before it gets big. And it nudges the daily decay drift back to the policy weights. Rebalancing is the boring part — and it's the part the next demo is about.

S10 (Close). That's the fund's investment strategy. Start from the index. Use leverage as efficiency, not as a louder bet. Bucket for all seasons. Tilt small, honestly. And rebalance to keep the policy honest. No prediction, no performance promise — just a rules-based structure you can run for a hundred years. Up next, the rebalancing strategy that keeps it all on rails.
